title: Deploy smoke runs the deployed commit's code with VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET on any successful deployment_status, with no fork, creator or trusted-ref guard
description:
The `smoke` job in .github/workflows/deploy-smoke.yml (at 539abe2) runs on every `deployment_status` event. Its `if:` only requires state == 'success' and a non-empty environment_url or target_url (lines 30-34). It has no creator, head-repository, fork or trusted-ref condition and no `environment:` approval gate. The secret-bearing jobs in db-checks.yml (line 79) and deriva.yml do have such a guard: they skip pull_request runs whose head repository is not this one.

VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET is placed in job-level env (line 41), so every step sees it. actions/checkout (line 61) has no `ref:`, so it checks out the event's GITHUB_SHA, which for deployment_status is the commit being deployed. The last step (line 100) then runs `node scripts/check_deploy.mjs` from that checkout. The AUD-01 host allowlist that is supposed to confine the secret lives inside the same checked-out script. Its production hosts are read from the same checkout's app.js (check_deploy.mjs:35-41). It therefore constrains only an honest commit. Even the honest script sends the secret as `x-vercel-protection-bypass` (line 61) to the deployment under test, and a fork-built preview of this Vercel project matches PREVIEW_DO_PROJETO (line 34).

I re-read every cited line at 539abe2 and confirmed each one. vercel.json has no git/github integration settings that would disable deployments. The retained hunter artifact agents/h07-deploy-edge/artifacts/check-05.out shows three things: the rendered `if:` has no guard tokens, there is no environment, and a fixture check_deploy.mjs that differs from main receives the dummy secret through the job env. No further local reproduction was decisive: the source path is complete and unrefuted.

Whether a lower-trust actor can actually reach this job is unobserved, and so is what it would get. That depends on four things. First, whether the Vercel GitHub integration is connected; CLAUDE.md:272 only instructs connecting it. Second, whether Vercel deploys fork pull requests, automatically or after a team member authorizes them under Git Fork Protection. Third, whether GitHub then raises a success deployment_status in this repository for the fork's sha and runs this workflow with repository secrets, and whether that run uses the default-branch workflow file or the one in the deployment commit. If it uses the deployment commit's file, exposure extends to every repository secret. Fourth, whether the repository is public: ADR-0003 says so, but run metadata reports it private. These are Vercel and GitHub hosted facts. The changelog downgraded AUD-01 because the URL comes from Vercel or from repository writers (docs/CHANGELOG.md:21). That rationale does not address who authored the commit being deployed and executed.
claimed_root_cause: A privileged deployment_status job trusts both the code and the deployment of whatever commit the event names. Secret confinement (the host allowlist in scripts/check_deploy.mjs, fed by HOSTS_PROD from the same checkout's app.js) is implemented in the checked-out deployment-commit code instead of in trusted workflow configuration. The job has no condition excluding deployments of commits not authored on this repository's own branches: no fork, creator or trusted-ref guard and no environment gate. Its sibling secret-bearing PR jobs do exclude forks.

trace.description: Any deployment_status event in the repository triggers the workflow. Whether the Vercel app creates one for an authorized or unprotected fork-PR preview, and with which sha, is a hosted fact (see blockers).
The guard checks only deployment_status.state == 'success' and a non-empty environment_url or target_url (lines 30-34). It has no creator, head-repository/fork or trusted-ref condition.
VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET is pulled from repository secrets into job-level env and is visible to every step. No `environment:` key requires reviewer approval.
Checkout sets only persist-credentials: false and no `ref:`, so it uses the event default (GITHUB_SHA). For deployment_status that is the commit being deployed.

Runs `node scripts/check_deploy.mjs` from that checkout while the secret is in the process environment. For a non-production deployment, DEPLOY_URL stays the deployment's own preview URL (lines 74-78).

The deployed commit's own script reads the secret. Its host allowlist (lines 34-40) comes from the same commit's app.js, so an altered commit is unconstrained. The unaltered script sends the secret as a request header (line 61) to the deployment built from that commit.

evidence.description: The sibling secret-bearing jobs exclude forks with `github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository`. deploy-smoke has no equivalent for deployment events.
HOSTS_PROD for the secret allowlist is read from the LOCAL (checked-out) app.js, the same commit whose deployment is being tested.

Every request to an allowlisted deployment carries `x-vercel-protection-bypass`. A fork-built preview of this project matches PREVIEW_DO_PROJETO (line 34), so it receives the secret even when the script is honest.
AUD-01 severity was lowered because the URL comes from Vercel or from repository writers. The author of the deployed and executed commit is not considered.
The decision record says the repository is public and stays public, so any GitHub user could open a fork pull request. Current visibility is unobserved; run metadata reports it private.

The Vercel-GitHub auto-deploy connection is described as a dashboard action to perform. Whether it is connected, and therefore whether Vercel emits deployment_status here at all, is not visible in the repository.
The AUD-01 regression suite only exercises the host allowlist inside a trusted copy of the script. Nothing covers the provenance of the commit the workflow checks out and executes.

blockers: Vercel project state, a dashboard fact absent from the repository: whether the GitHub integration is connected, and the Git Fork Protection setting (Project Settings > Security). The setting decides whether fork-PR previews deploy automatically or only after a team member authorizes them.

Whether the Vercel GitHub integration creates a GitHub Deployment and a success deployment_status in this repository for a fork-PR preview, and with which sha and ref. This is provider behavior that cannot be observed offline.

Whether GitHub Actions starts deployment_status workflows for such a fork-authored sha with repository secrets. Also whether it reads the workflow definition from the deployment commit, which would extend exposure from the bypass secret to every repository secret, or from the default branch. Both are hosted GitHub facts.

Current repository visibility and fork policy. ADR-0003 records the repository as public, while run metadata reports it private. This determines whether any GitHub user or only collaborators with read access can open a fork PR.

Whether Vercel forwards the `x-vercel-protection-bypass` request header to Functions or Middleware a fork could add to its own deployment. This decides the second leg: the secret reaching fork-built deployment code even if the checkout were pinned to trusted code.
Which deployments the configured Protection Bypass for Automation unlocks. This bounds the impact of disclosing it.

validation_plan.local: After a fix, re-run a policy rendering like agents/h07-deploy-edge check-05 (PyYAML over deploy-smoke.yml) inside the sandbox and assert three things. First, the step that holds VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET runs only code from a trusted ref, for example a second actions/checkout of the default branch for scripts/ and app.js, with the deployment commit never executed. Second, the secret is scoped to that single step's env, not job env. Third, the job either requires an `environment:` with required reviewers, or has an `if:` that admits only deployments whose creator is the Vercel app and whose sha is on a branch of this repository. Add a case to tests/deploy-smoke.test.js that fails if the workflow checks out the event commit while exposing the secret.
validation_plan.deployment:
Owner-observed only; do not probe anyone else's infrastructure.
1. In Vercel, read Project Settings > Git (is the GitHub repository connected?) and Settings > Security > Git Fork Protection.
2. In GitHub, confirm the repository's visibility and fork policy. In the Actions tab, open a past 'Deploy smoke' run triggered by deployment_status and note deployment.creator.login, deployment.sha and deployment.ref from the event payload.
3. From an owner-controlled second GitHub account, open a fork PR whose only change makes scripts/check_deploy.mjs print `Boolean(process.env.VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET)` and `git rev-parse HEAD`, never the value. Authorize the Vercel preview if prompted.
4. In the resulting 'Deploy smoke' run, check whether it was triggered by deployment_status, whether the checked-out sha is the fork commit, and whether the boolean is true.
5. To learn whether workflow definitions come from the deployment commit, the same fork commit may add a workflow `on: deployment_status` that prints only `${{ secrets.SUPABASE_TEST_AUDIT_DATABASE_URL != '' }}`.
6. Close the PR and delete the fork afterwards. Rotate the bypass secret, plus any secret shown as present to fork code.

title: Owner-only `postgres` backup credential can reach code from any ref an agent or other writer pushes or dispatches (repository secret, no environment or ref binding)
description: docs/backup.md:50-57 tells the owner to add SUPABASE_BACKUP_DATABASE_URL as a repository secret and says only the owner adds it and that the URI must never be sent to the agent/chat. The same page then names the agent as the one who dispatches the backup workflow. scripts/backup_private.py:45 accepts only the user `postgres.gontnlfmothfglssbyyk`, which is the owner role of the sole shared database, not a minimal read-only login. backup-private.yml runs on workflow_dispatch (line 6). Job `backup` (line 16) has no `environment:` and no condition on github.ref, and it passes the secret (line 70) to `python3 scripts/backup_private.py` (line 73) checked out from the dispatched ref. Every guard in the script (pooler/verify-full URL validation, age recipient regex at :125, fixed error messages, upload of the .age file only) is therefore code the dispatcher chooses, not a boundary. GitHub's model gives anyone who can run their own code in a workflow effective read access to repository secrets. There are three ways to do that: (a) push a branch that changes only scripts/backup_private.py, then dispatch backup-private.yml on that branch (needs Actions write); (b) open a same-repo PR or push a branch that adds or edits a workflow file referencing `${{ secrets.SUPABASE_BACKUP_DATABASE_URL }}` (pull_request runs at db-checks.yml:66 and deriva.yml:47 use the PR's own workflow definitions, and the fork-exclusion `if:` at db-checks.yml:79 does not exclude same-repo branches); (c) push a branch whose new workflow triggers on push. Path (c) has a precedent: CHANGELOG:1366-1369 records that the agent session could not dispatch workflows at the time, so the owner had a temporary workflow triggered by a branch push. That precedent shows agent-pushed workflow code ran in Actions. It does not show a privileged secret was received: backup.yml uses no secrets, only the public anon key. Code reached this way can print the URI in transformed form to beat log masking, connect with owner rights, or write a plaintext or self-keyed dump to the upload path (line 78). Who can read run logs and artifacts depends on repository visibility, which is unobserved: ADR-0003 records 'public', while GitHub metadata reportedly says private. SUPABASE_TEST_AUDIT_DATABASE_URL is exposed to same-repo PR code the same way (db-checks.yml:79-83, deriva.yml:60-64). This contradicts the claim in the phase3-security.yml:9 header that 'o secret não é exposto a PRs', but that credential is minimal, so its impact is low. Whether the gap is exploitable depends on GitHub panel state: where the secret is scoped, and the push, workflows and dispatch permissions of the agent identity and of any other writers.
claimed_root_cause: Two secrets that carry authority above a branch writer are stored at repository scope. The workflows that consume them take their code from a ref the caller selects: workflow_dispatch on any branch, same-repo pull_request, or a push to any branch. No GitHub Environment with a main-only deployment-branch policy and an owner reviewer binds them to reviewed code. So the documented boundary, that the agent dispatches but never receives the URI (docs/backup.md:53,57), is enforced by nothing in source. Under GitHub's model, every principal that can push code and run a workflow can read every repository secret.

trace.description: Manual dispatch with no inputs and no ref restriction. Job `backup` (line 16) declares no `environment:` and no `if:` on github.ref, so the workflow runs from whichever branch the dispatcher selects, and checkout (line 33) fetches that ref.

trace.scope: jobs.backup.steps['Dump, restauração, todas as contagens e criptografia'].env
trace.description: SUPABASE_BACKUP_DATABASE_URL (and BACKUP_AGE_PUBLIC_KEY at line 71) is injected into the step that runs `python3 scripts/backup_private.py` (line 73) from the dispatched ref. An earlier step (lines 36-43) also receives both secrets, but only checks that they are non-empty.

The script that exists on the caller's branch reads the raw URI from the environment. The age recipient check (line 125), URL validation, read-only snapshot and fixed error messages are all part of that caller-chosen file, so none of them constrains a modified copy.

The only credential accepted is user `postgres.<PROJECT_REF>` (PROJECT_REF=gontnlfmothfglssbyyk, line 19). That is the database owner role of the sole shared database, not a minimal read-only backup login.

Alternative path that needs no dispatch. A same-repo PR runs the workflow definitions from the PR head, and the fork-exclusion `if:` at line 79 lets same-repo branches through. A branch that adds `${{ secrets.SUPABASE_BACKUP_DATABASE_URL }}` to any job receives it, provided the pushing identity may modify .github/workflows. deriva.yml:47 behaves the same way, as does any new branch workflow triggered on push.

trace.scope: jobs.backup.steps['Publicar somente o pacote criptografado aprovado'].with.path
trace.description: The workflow uploads whatever file the caller's script leaves at this path as an artifact with 30-day retention. Anything the script prints goes to the run log. Either way the postgres credential, or a dump not encrypted to the owner's key, leaves the owner-only boundary and is readable by everyone who can read this repository's Actions runs (public or private visibility is unobserved).

evidence.description: Setup says 'Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret' for both backup secrets. The intended scope is repository-wide, not an environment.
Intended boundary: 'Só o dono cadastra; nunca enviar a URI ao agente/chat.'
'O agente dispara e acompanha o workflow.' The principal that must never receive the URI is the designated dispatcher.

At that time the agent session could not dispatch workflows ('nem consegue disparar o workflow Backup'). Lines 1367-1369: the owner's backup was produced by 'um workflow temporário disparado por push na branch'. So code from a pushed branch has run in this repository's Actions, which supports path (c). This precedent involved no privileged secret, because backup.yml uses only the public anon key.

Header claims the auditor secret 'não é exposto a PRs'. That holds only for this workflow: db-checks.yml:79-83 and deriva.yml:60-64 give SUPABASE_TEST_AUDIT_DATABASE_URL to same-repo PR-head code at job scope. This is a lower-impact variant of the same scoping gap.

The only branch control described is the main ruleset (required checks), and it 'não exige aprovação humana'. Nothing restricts which refs secret-bearing workflows run from, and no environment protection is described.
PROJECT_REF = "gontnlfmothfglssbyyk", the sole database that production and previews both use. Combined with line 45, the secret is that database's owner credential.

blockers: Not source-observable: whether SUPABASE_BACKUP_DATABASE_URL and BACKUP_AGE_PUBLIC_KEY are currently configured, and whether they are repository or organization secrets or are restricted to a GitHub Environment with deployment-branch and reviewer protection. docs/backup.md:50 says repository secret, and backup-private.yml declares no environment, so as written an environment-only secret would not even resolve.

Not source-observable: the GitHub identity and fine-grained permissions the AI agent sessions (Claude Code / Codex) use to push and dispatch: Contents write, Workflows permission to modify .github/workflows, and Actions write to dispatch on an arbitrary ref. Also whether other write-level collaborators or apps exist. CHANGELOG:1366 shows that dispatch was unavailable to the agent at one point, while docs/backup.md:57 says the agent now dispatches.
Not source-observable: repository or organization Actions policies, and branch or tag rulesets, that could restrict which refs or actors may run workflows or push workflow-file changes.

Not source-observable: the current repository visibility (ADR-0003 says public, GitHub metadata reportedly says private). It sets the audience for run logs and artifacts, but it does not change whether the agent or another writer can obtain the secret.

validation_plan.deployment: Owner, in the GitHub web UI, read-only: (1) Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions. Record whether SUPABASE_BACKUP_DATABASE_URL and BACKUP_AGE_PUBLIC_KEY are listed under Repository secrets or Organization secrets visible to this repo (finding holds), or only under an Environment that has a deployment-branch policy limited to main and the owner as required reviewer (finding does not hold). (2) Settings → Integrations (GitHub Apps) and Collaborators: record the Contents, Workflows and Actions permissions of the identity the agent sessions push and dispatch with, and list any other writers. (3) Settings → Actions → General and Rules: record any policy restricting workflow runs or workflow-file pushes by ref or actor. (4) Optional safe confirmation without the real secret: in a throwaway repository with a repository secret DUMMY=marker, have the agent identity push a branch whose script prints only the secret's length, then dispatch the workflow on that branch, or let a push-triggered workflow run it. A printed length proves that agent-chosen code receives repository secrets. Never run modified code against the real SUPABASE_BACKUP_DATABASE_URL. Remediation to verify afterwards: move both backup secrets into an Environment (for example `backup-integral`) limited to `main` with the owner as required reviewer, add `environment: backup-integral` to jobs.backup, rotate the postgres password if the scope was ever repository-wide while non-owner writers existed, and consider a dedicated read-only backup login instead of `postgres`.
validation_plan.local: Regression check after the fix. Statically render the trigger × secret × environment matrix for .github/workflows/*.yml, in the same way as agents/h17-ci-secrets/artifacts/check-02.out. Require jobs.backup in backup-private.yml to declare the protected environment. Require that no job reachable from pull_request, push to non-main branches, or an unrestricted workflow_dispatch references secrets.SUPABASE_BACKUP_DATABASE_URL or secrets.BACKUP_AGE_PUBLIC_KEY. Require the phase3-security.yml:9 claim either to be made true (move SUPABASE_TEST_AUDIT_DATABASE_URL in db-checks.yml and deriva.yml behind an environment, or off pull_request) or to be corrected. This is source parsing only and needs no secrets or network.

title: Anonymous Realtime subscriptions multiply owner bulk writes on the single shared Supabase project; only unobserved hosted quotas limit this
description: The anon JWT for project gontnlfmothfglssbyyk (role anon, exp 2036) is a literal in the public bundle and is used on every host. Anyone can therefore open Realtime WebSockets with it and join postgres_changes bindings on the 15 published tables. initRealtime shows the pattern: one public channel 'divat-rt' with 15 unfiltered event:'*' bindings, no private:true and no Realtime Authorization. Nothing in the repository limits how many connections, channels or duplicate bindings an anonymous client creates; opening many portal tabs already does this. RT_TABLES, which check_realtime.mjs requires to equal the live publication, includes the large tables itinerario_teste, qh_intervalo_teste and qh_predeterminado_teste. On 03/10/2026 one owner transaction inserted 52,385 + 9,553 + 25,748 = 87,686 rows into those tables. Routine loads are CSV imports through the Table Editor of 'what changed' (docs/etl.md:30-33), so their size and frequency are not evidenced. Supabase documents that postgres_changes checks each change against every matching subscription when RLS is enabled, as it is on every public table here. The number of authorization checks and delivered messages per owner write therefore grows linearly with the number of subscriptions an attacker holds. That work runs on the same database that serves every visitor's REST reads and counts against the project-wide Realtime connection and message allocation. The anon statement_timeout (an ALTER ROLE setting applied at login, not on SET ROLE) and pgrst.db_max_rows (PostgREST only) do not bound this path. eventsPerSecond:5 is only appended to the WebSocket URL by the client. Limits: the attacker cannot write data or choose when owner writes happen. Their cost is holding idle sockets with heartbeats. The portal falls back to REST without live updates if Realtime fails. This is exactly the comparable baseline (standard Supabase anon key + RLS + postgres_changes), which Supabase documents as scaling with subscriber count. That is calibration only. Whether hosted per-project quotas, internal poller timeouts or plan restrictions make the amplified cost material for this project cannot be observed from source.
claimed_root_cause: The portal exposes postgres_changes to the anonymous role on a publication that includes large, bulk-written tables. No repo-side control limits how many subscriptions there are: no private channel or realtime.messages authorization, no statement-level change signal replacing per-row changes, and no step that takes the large tables out of the publication during imports. check_realtime.mjs even requires them to stay published. The upstream per-subscription cost of each owner write therefore grows with the number of subscriptions an attacker chooses to hold. The only bounds are hosted per-project Realtime quotas and server internals that the repository neither sets nor records.

trace.scope: SUPABASE CONFIG: SB_KEY (same literal as SB_TESTE_KEY at line 175)
trace.description: Legacy anon JWT for gontnlfmothfglssbyyk (role anon, exp 2100831490 = 2036), shipped in the public bundle. SITE_USA_TESTE_TEMPORARIAMENTE = true (line 170) selects it for every host. Any anonymous party can use it to authenticate its own Realtime WebSockets.

Reference subscription shape: one public channel 'divat-rt' (line 1611, no private:true) with 15 unfiltered event:'*' postgres_changes bindings, one per RT_TABLES entry. Nothing in source limits a client to this shape. Repeating it across connections and channels, or binding the large tables several times, is limited only by hosted quotas.

eventsPerSecond:5 goes into realtime params. The vendored client only appends these to the socket URL (vendor/supabase-js-2.110.7.min.js:2 endPointURL; the bundle contains no eventsPerSecond logic). It is a hint chosen by the requester, not a server-side bound on postgres_changes delivery.

RT_TABLES lists itinerario_teste, qh_intervalo_teste and qh_predeterminado_teste. scripts/check_realtime.mjs:53 passes only when the live supabase_realtime publication equals RT_TABLES, so these large tables are kept in the publication on purpose. The historical baseline docs/backup_schema.sql:747-750 shows the same membership.

trace.scope: RLS enablement loop over public catalog tables
trace.description: RLS is enabled on every public table, and anon keeps SELECT USING (true) (baseline policy, e.g. docs/backup_schema.sql:646). Anon postgres_changes joins are therefore accepted. Under Supabase's documented design each change is RLS-checked once per matching subscription. That check runs on Realtime's own connection, so anon's login-time statement_timeout (docs/backup_schema.sql:786) and pgrst.db_max_rows (line 783) do not apply.

trace.scope: recovery DO block: INSERT INTO public.itinerario_teste (also lines 50 and 57)
trace.description: One owner transaction wrote 52,385 + 9,553 + 25,748 rows into published tables on the single shared project. Each row change is processed for every matching subscription, so the shared database and the project-wide Realtime allocation absorb work proportional to rows x attacker-held subscriptions. Routine Table Editor CSV imports (docs/etl.md:32-33) take the same path, at unevidenced size.

evidence.description: sbClient.channel('divat-rt') is created with no config: a public channel, no private:true, no Realtime Authorization. The anon key alone authorizes the join.

The Socket stores params (this.params=...) and endPointURL() calls appendParams(this.endPoint, this.params()). The bundle contains no occurrence of eventsPerSecond, so the 5/s value is not enforced on the client and an attacker's client can omit or raise it.
The only Realtime gate requires RT_TABLES == the live publication. It actively keeps the large tables published and inspects neither realtime.subscription cardinality nor quota usage.
Expected row counts 52,385 / 9,553 / 25,748 for the three published large tables, reinserted in one transaction (87,686 rows total).

The owner loads data by CSV import through the Supabase Table Editor. Line 33 says Realtime then updates open screens, and line 30 says the export contains 'what changed'. Writes to published tables are the normal operating mode; their typical size is not evidenced.

The historical baseline puts itinerario_teste (747), qh_intervalo_teste (749) and qh_predeterminado_teste (750) in supabase_realtime. Current membership is enforced via RT_TABLES and the check_realtime gate.
ALTER ROLE anon SET statement_timeout = '3s' applies when a session logs in as that role. It does not bound authorization work that Realtime's replication poller performs on its own connection.
Records 'o projeto está no plano Free, sem PITR' for an earlier project state. The current organization plan, and so the Realtime quotas, are not recorded in source.

blockers: Hosted Realtime limits for project gontnlfmothfglssbyyk are not in source: plan tier, max concurrent clients, max channels per client, max channel joins per second, max events/messages per second, and any per-tenant cap on postgres_changes subscriptions. The current plan is unverified; docs/CHANGELOG.md:1015 records Free only for an earlier state.

The hosted Realtime server is not in the repository; only the client is vendored. Its actual postgres_changes algorithm cannot be observed here: whether each joined binding becomes one realtime.subscription row, whether apply_rls runs one RLS check per subscription per WAL record or groups identical anon claims, and any internal statement_timeout or max_changes bound on list_changes. It must not be probed against the real project from the audit environment.

Billing and panel facts are unknown: whether delivered postgres_changes messages count against the project's Realtime message quota, whether the organization spend cap is on, and whether a Free-plan quota overrun restricts the whole project (including REST).

The real database and Realtime cost of the 03/10/2026 87,686-row recovery and of routine CSV imports, and the replication-slot lag they caused, are visible only in Supabase usage reports, logs and catalog views. The audit environment cannot read these, and it has no local Postgres or Supabase CLI to reproduce them.

validation_plan.local: Use an isolated local Supabase stack (supabase start) with its own throwaway anon key, never the real project. Create public.itinerario_teste with a primary key, enable RLS, add an anon SELECT USING (true) policy, and add the table to supabase_realtime. Set pg_stat_statements.track = 'all' so nested statements are visible. From a local supabase-js client using the throwaway anon key, open K postgres_changes bindings on that table (K = 1, 10, 100, 1000), spread across connections and channels up to the local quotas. Then run one INSERT of 10,000 rows. For each K, record: count(*) from realtime.subscription; total_exec_time and calls for realtime.list_changes and the nested walrus_rls_stmt / apply_rls statements; messages received by the clients; the time until the last message arrives; and pg_wal_lsn_diff(pg_current_wal_lsn(), confirmed_flush_lsn) for the realtime slot in pg_replication_slots. Also time a concurrent anon REST SELECT on another table during the drain. RLS executions and drain time that grow roughly linearly with K, together with measurable REST latency impact, confirm the amplification. Flat or grouped-per-claims cost refutes it.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner, in the Supabase dashboard only (read-only, no external probing): (1) record the organization plan, spend-cap state and the Project Settings > Realtime values (max concurrent clients, max events per second, max joins per second, channels per client, whether public channel access is allowed). (2) In Reports/Usage, read Realtime peak connections and messages, plus database CPU, around 03/10/2026 and the last few CSV imports. (3) In the SQL editor while the portal is idle, run read-only: select entity, count(*) from realtime.subscription group by entity; and select slot_name, active, pg_wal_lsn_diff(pg_current_wal_lsn(), confirmed_flush_lsn) from pg_replication_slots; to see live subscription cardinality and Realtime slot lag. (4) Check Realtime and Postgres logs during the last import for rate-limit, too-many-connections, or slow/timeout list_changes entries. Large quota headroom for anonymous connections, per-subscription authorization cost visible in logs or CPU, or slot lag during imports confirm the finding. Low enforced per-project caps, spend cap on with no project restriction, and negligible CPU/lag during imports downgrade it to hardening (no finding).

title: 'Atualizar baseline' says grave security findings cannot be baselined, but check_grants.mjs --atualizar-baseline writes them and the daily gate then passes
description: The dispatch-only workflow `Atualizar baseline` runs `node scripts/check_grants.mjs --atualizar-baseline` (atualizar-baseline.yml:103) and opens a PR with the diff. Its header (lines 19-21) and the PR body it generates (line 159) both say check_grants.mjs refuses to baseline the six grave indicators and exits 1 before writing. No such refusal exists, and none ever has. Line 163 filters findings only on severity 'erro', line 167 writes them all to scripts/security_baseline.json and line 170 exits 0. The read side (lines 173-186) honors any key in the file. The mechanics reproduce exactly. Every step, though, needs a trusted principal acting deliberately: a repository writer dispatches the workflow and the owner merges a PR whose diff names each grave finding. That actor can already edit the baseline or the script directly, so the path grants nobody a new capability. It produces no unauthorized disclosure, mutation, publication or execution.
claimed_root_cause: The --atualizar-baseline branch of check_grants.mjs filters only on severity and has no deny-list of non-baselinable types (rls_off, grant_escrita, grant_maintain, policy_escrita, funcao_public_execute, non-supabase_admin default privileges). The read side honors any baselined key. The workflow comment and PR body describe a refusal that was never implemented.

trace.description: The only trigger is a manual dispatch. It requires repository write access, so the actor is a trusted writer (or an agent acting for one), not a lower-trust principal.
Runs `node scripts/check_grants.mjs --atualizar-baseline` against the database through the auditor credential.
Anon/authenticated write grants become `grant_escrita` findings with severity 'erro'. rls_off (111), policy_escrita (129) and funcao_public_execute (135) are built the same way.

The only filter is `a.severidade === 'erro'`. All grave findings are written to security_baseline.json (167) and the process exits 0 (170). No type-based refusal exists in the current file or anywhere in its git history.

trace.scope: steps['Abrir o PR com o diff'] gh pr create --body
trace.description: The PR body falsely says the six grave indicators are refused, next to a diff and step summary (lines 115-125) that list the grave keys verbatim.
Only after a human merges, the baselined grave keys count as known exceptions. The gate exits 0 and still prints each one under 'Exceção conhecida'.

evidence.description: Asserted control: check_grants.mjs 'recusa e sai 1 antes de escrever' for the six grave indicators. This is false. It is the only place in the repo, besides line 159, that claims it.
The --atualizar-baseline block writes every severity-'erro' finding and exits 0. `git log --all -p -- scripts/check_grants.mjs` shows no grave or refusal logic ever added.

The script's own documented contract: --atualizar-baseline records an exception the operator DECIDED to accept, and a new write grant should be revoked, not baselined. Baselining is designed as a trusted human decision, not a guard.
The script header still says '--atualizar-baseline # SÓ LOCAL, nunca no CI', which contradicts the workflow. This is another documentation inconsistency, not a capability change.
The workflow never writes the branch. It opens a PR, and the merge is a second deliberate act by the owner, who sees the diff in the PR and in the step summary (lines 115-125).

Sandboxed reproduction with real script copies, a fake psql and a dummy auditor URL. The normal gate exits 1 listing grant_escrita, policy_escrita, rls_off and funcao_public_execute (lines 1-18). --atualizar-baseline exits 0 and writes those keys (lines 19-23). The normal gate then exits 0 'nenhum achado novo' (lines 24-33). The mechanics are confirmed. The rejection rests on actor and impact, not on mechanics.

reason: The mechanics reproduce (agents/v04-baseline-refusal/artifacts/check-01.out). Refuted for missing meaningful security impact and no lower-trust actor. Both companion validation rules (SUPPLY-CHAIN #1, DATA-ISOLATION #1) require a lower-trust principal and an unauthorized outcome caused by the path, and neither exists. (1) workflow_dispatch requires repository write access. The PR is merged by the owner. That same principal can already edit scripts/security_baseline.json or scripts/check_grants.mjs directly, so the missing refusal gives nobody a new capability. The contents/pull-requests write token is used only to push a new branch and open a PR, so there is no automation-identity overreach. (2) No lower-trust principal can cause the grave state: anon and authenticated cannot change grants, RLS or default privileges. It comes only from the owner or platform actions, and the anonymous-write exposure in that state is a separate root cause that exists whatever the gate says. (3) Until a human merges, the gate does its job: it exits 1 and prints 'REVOGUE o privilégio'. The PR diff and step summary list each grave key with its detail ('anon tem INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE em …'). Even after the merge, the gate prints each one as a known exception every day. The effect is a false assurance sentence shown to a trusted approver, sitting next to the truthful diff. That is a documentation and hardening defect in a detective control, not a vulnerability. As non-finding hardening, it is still worth fixing as the hunter proposed: implement the deny-list on the write and read sides with rig cases, or at minimum correct atualizar-baseline.yml:19-21 and :159 and check_grants.mjs:24. Calibration: the comparable anon-key + RLS SPA has no such gate at all. This was noted only as calibration, not as grounds for rejection.

title: The auditor DB credential can be sent over unauthenticated TLS (sslmode=require), so an impersonating peer receives it in cleartext
description: scripts/lib/audit-database.mjs is the only transport for the CI auditor credential SUPABASE_TEST_AUDIT_DATABASE_URL. The credential is injected at db-checks.yml:83/101/131, deriva.yml:64, phase3-security.yml:66 and atualizar-baseline.yml:100. The gates check_realtime, check_data_quality, check_grants, check_deriva and check_phase3_audit, plus atualizar-baseline, all reach psql through carregarConfiguracaoAuditora. validarConexaoAuditora accepts sslmode=require, and executarConsulta hands it to psql as PGSSLMODE. The child env is rebuilt from scratch with no PGSSLROOTCERT, PGREQUIREAUTH or PGCHANNELBINDING, and no workflow provisions a root certificate. Under require with no root.crt, libpq encrypts the connection but does not authenticate the server. It also answers whatever authentication method the peer requests. A peer that can stand in for db.gontnlfmothfglssbyyk.supabase.co (or the pooler host) through DNS or routing control can present any certificate, request AuthenticationCleartextPassword, and receive the divat_auditor_ci password. The verifier reproduced this independently. The real module, run with psql 16.15 under sslmode=require, sent a dummy password to a loopback peer presenting a self-signed CN=attacker.invalid certificate. In the same run, verify-full and verify-ca sent nothing. The live secret's sslmode is not directly observable. Two facts at the pinned commit establish that it is require. docs/seguranca.md §9.5 says refusing require would turn the four mandatory checks red. And with no root certificate provisioned anywhere, verify-ca and verify-full abort before authentication, as observed locally, so only require can work on a stock runner. The sibling privileged path, scripts/backup_private.py, forces verify-full against system roots.
root_cause: SSLMODES_ACEITOS (audit-database.mjs:37) includes 'require', and executarConsulta (lines 122-132) passes the chosen mode to libpq. It sets no PGSSLROOTCERT and pins no Supabase CA, and it sets no PGREQUIREAUTH or PGCHANNELBINDING. The control meant to bind the credential to the real Supabase endpoint therefore fails open in two places: server certificate verification, and the authentication method the client will answer. 'verify-ca' is also accepted. It does verify a chain, but not the hostname, so it is weaker than verify-full. It is not the decisive mode here, because without a configured root it fails closed.
intended_behavior: The auditor credential should be released only to a server that has proved it is the Supabase endpoint for gontnlfmothfglssbyyk. That means sslmode=verify-full against a pinned, versioned Supabase CA passed through PGSSLROOTCERT, matching the verify-full posture in scripts/backup_private.py:59,153. Password exposure should also be bounded by refusing cleartext and MD5 authentication (PGREQUIREAUTH=scram-sha-256), with channel binding required where the endpoint supports it.

trace.description: The repository secret SUPABASE_TEST_AUDIT_DATABASE_URL is injected into the gate job on a GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest runner. The same injection appears at db-checks.yml:101 and :131, deriva.yml:64, phase3-security.yml:66 and atualizar-baseline.yml:100. No step provisions a PostgreSQL root certificate.
The gate loads the credential through carregarConfiguracaoAuditora(). The other gates do the same at check_data_quality.mjs:85, check_deriva.mjs:95, check_grants.mjs:55 and check_phase3_audit.mjs:66.
Reads env[ENV_VAR] and passes it to validarConexaoAuditora.
The only transport check is membership in SSLMODES_ACEITOS (line 37: require, verify-ca, verify-full). 'require' passes, with no root certificate and no auth-method requirement.
Returns a frozen config carrying the password and sslmode='require'.

Spawns psql with a freshly built env: PGPASSWORD (line 128) and PGSSLMODE=require, with no PGSSLROOTCERT, PGREQUIREAUTH or PGCHANNELBINDING. libpq completes TLS with any server certificate and sends the password in a PasswordMessage when the peer requests cleartext authentication.

evidence.description: SSLMODES_ACEITOS = new Set(['require', 'verify-ca', 'verify-full']). An unauthenticated TLS mode is accepted.
The module's documented security contract presents 'require' as acceptable transport for the credential.
The test loop asserts that sslmode=require is accepted, so the fail-open mode is part of the guarded contract.

§9.5 (AUD-02) records that the validator accepts require, 'que cifra sem conferir o certificado'. It adds that refusing require without changing the secret would turn the realtime, seguranca, deriva and qualidade checks red, so the live secret relies on require.
The sibling privileged credential path forces PGSSLMODE=verify-full and PGSSLROOTCERT=system regardless of the URL. This is the stronger control the auditor path lacks.
Impact bound: the auditor login is asserted to have no direct table SELECT. What leaks is a minimal but persistent login to the shared database, valid until rotated.

Verifier reproduction. With the real module and psql 16.15 under sslmode=require, the loopback peer (self-signed CN=attacker.invalid) logged TLSv1.3, startup_user divat_auditor_ci, msg_type 'p' and password_received 'DUMMY-V02-REQUIRE'. Lines 13-14 are the verify-full and verify-ca controls: TLS aborted and no password was received. Line 4 shows the validator accepting the real host with sslmode=require.

conditions.description: The SUPABASE_TEST_AUDIT_DATABASE_URL secret uses sslmode=require. The value itself is unobservable. docs/seguranca.md:147-154 records this, and source implies it: no root certificate is provisioned in any workflow and executarConsulta sets no PGSSLROOTCERT, so verify-ca and verify-full abort on a stock runner. The runner also has no ~/.postgresql/root.crt, which is the default on GitHub-hosted images.

The attacker can intercept or redirect TCP traffic, or DNS resolution, between a GitHub-hosted runner and db.gontnlfmothfglssbyyk.supabase.co or the Supabase pooler. The gates run on a schedule, on dispatch, and on same-repo PRs.

libpq from postgresql-client 16 on ubuntu-latest: under sslmode=require with no root certificate it does not verify the server, and with require_auth unset it answers AuthenticationCleartextPassword. Observed locally with psql 16.15.

execution.attacker_perspective: An on-path network or DNS attacker between the CI runner and Supabase poses as the PostgreSQL server for db.gontnlfmothfglssbyyk.supabase.co, presents any self-signed certificate, and requests cleartext password authentication.
payloads: Fake peer: reply 'S' to SSLRequest; TLS handshake with self-signed CN=attacker.invalid; after StartupMessage send AuthenticationCleartextPassword = b'R' + int32(8) + int32(3)
Controls: the same URL with sslmode=verify-full and with sslmode=verify-ca
instructions: Inside the OS sandbox (uid 65534, new network namespace with loopback only, read-only target, HOME without .postgresql/root.crt), generate a self-signed certificate for CN=attacker.invalid with /usr/bin/openssl.

Start scratch/peer.py on 127.0.0.1:54331. For each connection it answers SSLRequest with 'S', wraps TLS, parses the StartupMessage, requests AuthenticationCleartextPassword, logs any PasswordMessage, then sends an ErrorResponse.

In scratch/harness.mjs, import the real validarConexaoAuditora and executarConsulta from /home/user/DETRO-Banco-de-Dados/scripts/lib/audit-database.mjs. Validate the payload URL and confirm it is accepted with sslmode=require.
Call executarConsulta with the validated config, changing only host/port to 127.0.0.1:54331 to stand in for DNS or route redirection, with psqlBin=/usr/bin/psql (16.15).
Repeat with sslmode=verify-full and sslmode=verify-ca as controls.
execution.observed_result: The validator accepted host db.gontnlfmothfglssbyyk.supabase.co with sslmode=require. The fake peer logged sslrequest=true, TLSv1.3, startup_user divat_auditor_ci, msg_type 'p' and password_received 'DUMMY-V02-REQUIRE'. executarConsulta then threw AuditDatabaseError (status 2). In both controls (verify-full, verify-ca) the client aborted TLS (SSLEOFError at the peer) and no password was received. Promoted as agents/v02-sslmode/artifacts/check-01.out.

remediation.strategy: Accept only sslmode=verify-full. Version the public Supabase CA certificate in the repo and always pass it to psql through PGSSLROOTCERT. Always set PGREQUIREAUTH=scram-sha-256, which stops cleartext and MD5 password disclosure on its own. Set PGCHANNELBINDING=require if the endpoint supports it, after confirming that in a manual dispatch run. Following docs/seguranca.md §9.5, validate the new CA path in a manual run first, then switch the secret to verify-full, then refuse require, and then rotate the divat_auditor_ci password. Regression tests: replace the 'require is accepted' loop in tests/audit-database.test.mjs with assertions that require and verify-ca are refused, and that the env given to psql contains PGSSLMODE=verify-full, PGSSLROOTCERT and PGREQUIREAUTH=scram-sha-256. Add a loopback fake-peer test asserting that no PasswordMessage reaches an unverified peer.

code_changes.fixed_code:
const SSLMODES_ACEITOS = new Set(['verify-full']);
const SUPABASE_CA = new URL('./supabase-ca.crt', import.meta.url).pathname; // certificado público versionado
// em executarConsulta, env do psql:
      PGSSLMODE: 'verify-full',
      PGSSLROOTCERT: SUPABASE_CA,
      PGREQUIREAUTH: 'scram-sha-256',
      PGCHANNELBINDING: 'require', // só após confirmar suporte do endpoint em run manual

likelihood.reason: Requires an on-path or DNS-level position between a GitHub-hosted runner and Supabase, which is hard to obtain. The credential is exercised on a schedule and on same-repo PRs, which widens the window but does not lower that bar.

impact.reason: Exposes a protected CI secret: a persistent login to the shared, sole production database, valid until rotated. divat_auditor_ci is minimal: audit diagnostics and catalog metadata, with no direct table SELECT (asserted at check_phase3_audit.mjs:50) and no writes. The gain is metadata disclosure and resource use within the role's limits.

confidence.reason: The fail-open transport is source-visible, and the verifier reproduced it independently against the real module and psql 16.15, with verify-full and verify-ca controls. The live secret's sslmode is not directly observed. It is established by docs/seguranca.md §9.5 and by the absence of any root certificate provisioning, which makes require the only accepted mode that can work on a stock runner.
